chunks: Draw a half-bridge circuit. The question: Draw a half-bidge circuit.
A half-bridge is two switches in series between the supply and ground, with the output taken from the node between them. When the top switch is on, the output is at the supply.
When the bottom one is on, it is at ground. Flip between them quickly, and the average output is the fraction of time the top is on, times the supply.
Picture flicking a mixer handle very fast between hot and cold. If hot is on a quarter of the time, the water comes out a quarter of the way from cold to hot.
The duty cycle sets the average. Never open both taps at once into the same pipe: that connects the hot supply straight to the cold drain. In a half-bridge, that is shoot-through.
Two ideal switches from V M to ground; the node between them is the output. A load connects from SW to ground (or elsewhere, see below).
Switch node: the junction between the two switches. It is the output. Duty cycle ( D ): the fraction of each period the high side is on. Average output is D V M .
Dead time: a short gap with both switches off between transitions, so they never overlap. Body diode: the diode built into each MOSFET (transistor switch).
It carries the load current during dead time. Inductive load: a load with a coil, like a motor, whose current cannot change instantly.
With a 12 volts supply and a 25% duty cycle, the output averages 0. 25 times 12 equals 3 volts. Put a motor with 1 millihenries of inductance on it, switching at 20 kilohertz.
Its coil smooths the current, which wiggles by only about 0. 11 amps each cycle. With 100 nanoseconds of dead time on each edge, 5 amps flowing through a 0.
7 volts body diode wastes only 0. 7 times 5 times 200 nanoseconds times 20 kilohertz equals 14 milliwatts. That is the whole idea.
"A half-bridge is two switches in series from the supply to ground, with the output at the middle node.
High side on gives the supply, low side on gives ground, both off lets an inductive load clamp through a body diode.
I'd use two NFETs with body diodes, a bootstrapped gate driver for the high side, and dead time so the two never overlap.
The average output is duty cycle times supply, and with an LC filter it becomes a buck converter."
